area.title: Upload documents
area.scope: The upload documents page and the accompanying-document record: document types, reference and date of issue, attachments and their limits, the virus scan and its states, listing, viewing, downloading and removing documents, the uploader handshake and file storage. Stops at how documents show on the review page.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.
claims.quote: Now we need to be really careful here because the prototype isn't accessible. It's not using some GDS stuff. It's using prototype thrown up by AI stuff. ... the prototype isn't necessarily production-grade with its solution.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.
claims.quote: only use a version of auto complete or search or whatever that has been deemed accessible and meets our requirements. If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam says the content of a search dropdown (such as which countries a country dropdown holds) is not settled by 'the frontend is correct' and may need more input.
claims.quote: The content of that dropdown, if it's a country dropdown, what's in it? That might still need a bit more input, so it isn't as blunt to say the frontend is correct on this

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and is not to be blindly replicated by adding lots of JavaScript to the frontend, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: the prototype is doing stuff with JavaScript that is not GDS compliant. This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend. ... 'Do things like add all this JavaScript stuff for accessibility concerns and maintainability concerns.'

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: A behaviour the prototype gives with JavaScript is built only if it passes these tests in order: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns first; then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); otherwise it goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.quote: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns are used first. Where they have nothing, another tested government library is used, such as the Ministry of Justice's, HMRC's or the Scottish Government's. Where neither has anything, the behaviour goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.note: Marked 'Sam (point 3)'. HMRC is named in claim 5 but not in Sam's quote, which names Ministry of Justice and Scottish Government only; the examples are illustrative ('like').

claims.statement: A DR1 judgement on the same difference overrides the prototype default.

claims.statement: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default; the ruling names persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour as such constraints.
claims.quote: a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. The quote says 'auth'; claim 6 reads it as authentication. Claim 6 adds 'such as', making the list examples; the quote's parenthesis can be read either as examples or as the full list.

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled; the real persistence, validation and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express

claims.statement: POST /notifications/{ref}/document-uploads starts an accompanying-document upload session for a notification and answers 201 Created with a body holding uploadId and uploadUrl.
The 201 response from initiating an upload carries a Location header of the backend base URL (trailing slash removed) followed by /document-uploads/{uploadId}.
claims.quote: return URI.create(baseUrl + "/document-uploads/" + uploadId);

claims.statement: The uploadUrl returned on initiation points at the backend's own POST /document-uploads/{uploadId}/file endpoint, so the frontend uploads the file through the backend rather than straight to cdp-uploader.
claims.quote:
Points at this backend's own {@code POST /document-uploads/{uploadId}/file} endpoint so
   * the frontend (and the IT test assertions) use the backend as the upload target rather than
   * reaching cdp-uploader directly.
claims.note: The OpenAPI description of uploadUrl in DocumentUploadResponse still says 'URL of the cdp-uploader form to which the user should be redirected', which no longer matches the behaviour.

claims.statement: The document type (documentType) is required when initiating an upload and must be one of the DocumentType values.
The document reference (documentReference, the reference printed on the document) is required and must not be blank.
The document reference may be at most 100 characters long.
claims.quote: @Size(max = 100)

claims.statement: The document reference may contain only letters and digits: no spaces, slashes, hyphens or other punctuation.
claims.quote: @Pattern(regexp = "^[a-zA-Z0-9]*$")
claims.note: AccompanyingDocumentDtoTest builds an entity with documentReference "ITAHC/2026/001", which this API rule would refuse; the unit test bypasses validation.

claims.statement: The date of issue (dateOfIssue, the date on the physical document) is required and is a calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form.
The date of issue has no range check: the backend accepts any valid calendar date, past or future, because the request declares no past or future constraint.
claims.quote:
@NotNull
    @Schema(description = "Date of issue on the physical document",

claims.statement: A document-upload request that breaks a field rule is refused with 400, title "Validation Error", detail "Validation failed for one or more fields", and an errors map keyed by field name; the per-field messages are the validation framework's defaults because the request declares no custom messages.
claims.note: No test in this slice drives a document validation failure; user-facing error copy for the document fields does not live in the backend.

claims.statement: A document-upload request whose body cannot be read, such as a date of issue not in YYYY-MM-DD form or an unknown document type, is refused with 400, title "Malformed Request", and a fixed detail message.
claims.quote:
"Request body could not be read. Check the JSON is well-formed, that each date-only "
                + "field is a date, for example 2026-12-12, and that each timestamp is an "
                + "RFC 3339 instant, for example 2026-12-12T00:00:00Z"
claims.note: That an unknown documentType lands here rather than in field validation is inferred from it being an enum bound by the JSON parser.

claims.statement: Initiating an upload does not check that the notification exists: the OpenAPI annotation promises 404 "Notification not found", but the service never looks the notification up, and the IT gets 201 for a reference it never created.
claims.quote: @ApiResponse(responseCode = "404", description = "Notification not found", content = @Content)

claims.statement: Initiating an upload is not idempotent: every call creates a new cdp-uploader session, and a notification may hold several PENDING documents at once so a user can add a second document while the first is still being scanned.
claims.quote: This method is not idempotent. cdp-uploader is always called to create a * new upload session. Multiple PENDING documents are deliberately permitted per notification — * the UX supports adding a second document while the first is still being scanned.

claims.statement: A newly initiated document is saved against the notification reference with its type, reference and date of issue, scan status PENDING and an empty file list.
claims.quote:
.documentType(request.documentType())
        .documentReference(request.documentReference())
        .dateOfIssue(request.dateOfIssue())
        .scanStatus(ScanStatus.PENDING)
        .files(new ArrayList<>())

claims.statement: If cdp-uploader hands back an uploadId that is already stored, initiation is refused with 409, title "Resource Conflict", and no record is saved for that session.
claims.quote:
throw new ConflictException(
          "Upload session with id " + document.getUploadId() + " already exists");

claims.statement: If cdp-uploader answers the initiate call with a non-2xx status, initiation fails with 502, title "Upstream Service Error", detail "cdp-uploader returned an error response: HTTP {status}".
claims.quote:
throw new ServiceUnavailableException(
                    "cdp-uploader returned an error response: HTTP " + statusCode);

claims.statement: If cdp-uploader cannot be reached during initiation (connection refused, timeout, DNS failure), initiation fails with 502 and detail beginning "cdp-uploader is unreachable: ".
claims.quote: throw new ServiceUnavailableException("cdp-uploader is unreachable: " + e.getMessage(), e);

claims.statement: Initiation calls cdp-uploader's /initiate endpoint with a redirect, a callback URL, the documents S3 bucket, an S3 path equal to the notification reference, the maximum file size, the allowed MIME types and a metadata map.
claims.quote:
CdpUploaderInitiateRequest initiateRequest = new CdpUploaderInitiateRequest(
        CDP_UPLOADER_REDIRECT_PATH,
        buildCallbackUrl(),
        cdpConfig.s3().documentsBucket(),
        notificationRef,
        cdpConfig.uploader().maxFileSize(),
        cdpConfig.uploader().mimeTypes(),
        buildMetadata(notificationRef, request, correlationId));

claims.statement: The scan-result callback URL given to cdp-uploader is fixed as the backend base URL followed by /document-uploads/pending/scan-results, with the literal word pending in place of an upload id.
claims.quote: return backendBaseUrl + "/document-uploads/pending/scan-results";

claims.statement: The metadata sent to cdp-uploader holds the notification reference, the document type, the document reference and a new random correlationId minted per upload; the date of issue is not sent.

The redirect given to cdp-uploader is always the relative path "/" and is never shown to the user, because the file is posted to cdp-uploader by the server and cdp-uploader's redirect response is ignored.
claims.quote:
Our flow is server-proxied (the frontend POSTs the file to
   * cdp-uploader on the user's behalf and ignores cdp-uploader's 302 response), so the value is
   * never user-visible

claims.statement: The maximum file size passed to cdp-uploader defaults to 52428800 bytes (50 MB) and can be changed with CDP_UPLOADER_MAX_FILE_SIZE.
claims.quote: max-file-size: ${CDP_UPLOADER_MAX_FILE_SIZE:52428800}

claims.statement: The file types cdp-uploader is told to allow default to PDF, Word (.doc and .docx), JPEG, PNG and Excel (.xls and .xlsx), and can be changed with CDP_UPLOADER_MIME_TYPES.
claims.quote: mime-types: ${CDP_UPLOADER_MIME_TYPES:application/pdf,application/msword,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document,image/jpeg,image/png,application/vnd.ms-excel,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet}

Deliberately omits {@code s3Key} and {@code s3Bucket} — these are internal S3 storage

POST /document-uploads/{upload-id}/scan-results receives cdp-uploader's antivirus scan result and answers 204 No Content once it is recorded.

A scan result is matched to its document by the correlationId in the callback's metadata, not by the upload id in the URL, so a callback to /document-uploads/pending/scan-results updates the right document.

claims.statement: A document's scan status becomes COMPLETE only when the scan result reports zero rejected files; any other count, or a missing count, makes it REJECTED (fail closed).

Fail-closed: treat a missing or non-zero rejected count as REJECTED to avoid silently
   * accepting a file when cdp-uploader omits the field.

Scan status PENDING means the file has been uploaded (or the session started) and is awaiting antivirus scanning.

@Schema(description = "Antivirus scan completed successfully — file is clean")

claims.statement: Scan status REJECTED means the antivirus scan rejected the file (virus or malware detected).
claims.quote:
@Schema(description = "Antivirus scan rejected the file (virus or malware detected)")
  REJECTED

claims.statement: File status COMPLETE (sent by cdp-uploader as "complete") means the file was scanned and is clean.
File status REJECTED (sent by cdp-uploader as "rejected") means the antivirus scan rejected the file.
A file's status is set once, from the scan result: there is no pending file status, because a file entry only exists after a scan result arrives.
claims.quote: /** Individual file entries populated by cdp-uploader callbacks. Initialised to empty list. */

{@code s3Key} follows the pattern {@code "{uploadId}/{fileId}"} for complete files and is

'document scan settled': isScanned,
    'document scan not rejected': (listed) => !scanWasRejected(listed)

claims.statement: The document scan is held to a P99 under 60 seconds, the same allowance as upload pages.
claims.quote: 'Document scan allowance: P99 under 60s, as for upload pages (DR-EUDP-005 section 4.7, SYN-28, SYN-29)'

claims.statement: The documents page is left by submitting action=continue; with no documents to add, the page is only opened and continued.
claims.quote: walker.submit(page, { action: 'continue' }, ENDPOINTS.save)

claims.statement: How many documents a live-animals notification uploads is drawn from the traffic model's documentsPerNotification distribution, and each file's type and size are drawn from the model's documentTypes and documentKilobytes.
claims.quote: documents: countAt(iteration, journeyModel.documentsPerNotification)

claims.statement: Each uploaded document's reference is written PERFDOC<vu>V<iteration>N<document number>, letters and digits only.
claims.quote:
const referenceFor = ({ vu, iteration }, number) =>
  `PERFDOC${vu}V${iteration}N${number}`

claims.statement: On a local run, document storage and virus scanning are the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan, so scan results there are not CDP's.
claims.quote: Stand-ins: SNS and SQS are floci, and document storage and virus scanning are the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan, so results that depend on them are not CDP's

sources.role: how the real animals frontend renders today

claims.statement: The trader reaches the document upload page from the overview's 'Upload documents' task link, which is followed once origin, commodities and commodity details have been completed; it lives at /live-animals/notifications/{notification reference}/accompanying-documents.
claims.quote: Upload documents
claims.note: Every trace in the part unlocks sections (origin, commodities, commodity details) before following the link; whether the link is available before that is not shown here.

claims.statement: The page's browser title is 'Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: When the page re-renders with validation errors its browser title is prefixed with 'Error: '.
claims.quote: Error: Upload documents - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The page's main heading (H1, govuk-heading-l) is 'Upload documents', under the section caption 'Documents' (govuk-caption-l).
claims.quote: Documents / Upload documents

claims.statement: Above the caption the page shows a blue 'Draft' tag and the notification reference (for example GBN-AG-26-6B6EC5) in a strip that uses the non-govuk class app-journey-strip.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2849 main (classes: app-journey-strip, govuk-tag--blue)
claims.quote: Draft GBN-AG-26-6B6EC5

claims.statement: The page has a 'Back' link (govuk-back-link) pointing at the notification overview; following it shows the 'Overview' heading.
claims.quote: Back

claims.statement: The page holds one POST form, submitted as multipart/form-data with browser validation turned off (novalidate), carrying the maximum file size (10000000 bytes) and the oversize message as data attributes.
claims.quote: "enctype":"multipart/form-data","novalidate":"","data-max-file-size":"10000000","data-oversize-error":"The selected file must be smaller than 10MB"

claims.statement: The form carries a hidden CSRF token field named crumb.
claims.quote: <input type=hidden name=crumb value=[REDACTED]>

claims.statement: The form carries a hidden concurrencyToken field (value 0 on a new notification), which reads as an optimistic-concurrency check on the save.
claims.quote: <input type=hidden name=concurrencyToken value=0>
claims.note: Purpose inferred from the field name; no trace in this part exercises a concurrency conflict.

claims.statement: The add-a-document fields sit inside a section labelled by an H2 'File upload', exposed as a region named 'File upload'.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-a24dd call@2915; snapshot SECTION aria-labelledby=file-upload-heading
claims.quote: File upload

claims.statement: The 'File upload' region is built from the GOV.UK summary card component (govuk-summary-card, __title-wrapper, __title, __content) used as a container for form fields rather than for a summary list.
claims.quote: SECTION {"class":"govuk-summary-card","aria-labelledby":"file-upload-heading"}
claims.note: A non-standard use of a govuk-frontend component: a summary card normally wraps a summary list.

claims.statement: The 'File upload' region contains the Document reference, Document type and Date of issue fields, the Attachment upload control and the 'Save and add another' button.
claims.quote: region[name="File upload"] >> label="Document reference" / "Document type" / "Date of issue" / button[name="Attachment"] / button[name="Save and add another"]

claims.statement: The page actions ('Save and continue' and the rest of the button group) sit outside the 'File upload' region: the region contains no 'Save and continue' button, while the page has one.
claims.quote: region[name="File upload"] >> button[name="Save and continue"] toHaveCount(0)

claims.statement: The first field is a text input 'Document reference' (name accompanyingDocumentReference, width-20, small label), empty by default.
claims.quote: Document reference

claims.statement: The Document reference field's hint, set as its accessible description, is 'For example, GBHC1234567890.'.
claims.quote: For example, GBHC1234567890.

claims.statement: The second field is a select 'Document type' (name accompanyingDocumentType, govuk-select) whose value is empty by default.
claims.quote: Document type

claims.statement: The Document type select starts with the placeholder option 'Select one' (empty value) followed by fourteen document types, with these values and labels in this order: ITAHC 'Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)', VETERINARY_HEALTH_CERTIFICATE 'Veterinary health certificate', AIR_WAYBILL 'Air waybill', IMPORT_PERMIT 'Import permit', LETTER_OF_AUTHORITY 'Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC)', COMMERCIAL_INVOICE 'Commercial invoice', SEA_WAYBILL 'Sea waybill', RAIL_WAYBILL 'Rail waybill', BILL_OF_LADING 'Bill of lading', CATCH_CERTIFICATE 'Catch certificate', LABORATORY_SAMPLING_RESULTS_FOR_AFLATOXIN 'Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793)', HEALTH_CERTIFICATE 'Health certificate', JOURNEY_LOG 'Journey log', OTHER 'Other'.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-5906a call@2989; options read from trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2849
claims.quote: Select one | Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) | Veterinary health certificate | Air waybill | Import permit | Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC) | Commercial invoice | Sea waybill | Rail waybill | Bill of lading | Catch certificate | Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793) | Health certificate | Journey log | Other

claims.statement: In document order the fields are Document reference, then Document type, then Date of issue: the type select sits between the reference and the date.
claims.quote: #accompanyingDocumentReference, #accompanyingDocumentType, #accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue

claims.statement: The third field is a text input 'Date of issue' (name accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue, width-10, autocomplete off) enhanced by the MOJ date picker component (moj-datepicker), typed as a single dd/mm/yyyy string.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2849 #accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue; values filled 03/01/2026 and 12/12/2025
claims.quote: Date of issue
claims.note: A single text input with a date picker rather than the GOV.UK date input (day/month/year) component.

claims.statement: The Date of issue field's hint, set as its accessible description, is 'For example, 12/12/2025'.
claims.quote: For example, 12/12/2025

claims.statement: Once scripts run, the Date of issue input gains a 'Choose date' toggle button (visually hidden text) that opens the date picker dialog (aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-controls=datepicker-accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue).
claims.quote: Choose date

claims.statement: The date picker dialog (role dialog, aria-modal) opens on the current month, headed with the month and year (for example 'October 2026'), with today's date selected and marked current, previous/next month and year buttons, weekday headings Mon to Sun, a calendar grid of day buttons, and 'Select' and 'Close' buttons.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-01ae3 call@3249 DIV#datepicker-accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue; buttons read from trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 rendered DOM
claims.quote: October 2026 ... Previous year / Previous month / Next month / Next year ... Select / Close

claims.statement: The fourth field is a file upload labelled 'Attachment' (name file) that accepts .pdf, .doc, .docx, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .xls and .xlsx.
claims.quote: .pdf,.doc,.docx,.jpeg,.jpg,.png,.xls,.xlsx

claims.statement: With scripts running, the upload control the trader reaches is a button named 'Attachment' (the GOV.UK enhanced file upload); the real file input is hidden behind it.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-a24dd call@2923; DOM BUTTON#file aria-labelledby=file-label file-comma file, INPUT#file-input hidden
claims.quote: button[name="Attachment"]
claims.note: The drop zone itself is part 24's.

claims.statement: The Attachment hint opens with the bold line 'Your file must be:' followed by a bulleted list.
claims.quote: Your file must be:

claims.statement: The first upload constraint bullet states the size limit: 'smaller than 10MB'.
claims.quote: smaller than 10MB

claims.statement: The second upload constraint bullet lists the allowed file types.
claims.quote: a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX

claims.statement: The third upload constraint bullet states the document limit: 'up to a maximum of 15 files'.
claims.quote: up to a maximum of 15 files

claims.statement: The fourth upload constraint bullet says ZIP files are refused.
claims.quote: ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons

claims.statement: The document-limit bullet stays on the page once a document has been saved, so the trader still sees the total with rows present.
claims.quote: up to a maximum of 15 files

claims.statement: Inside the 'File upload' region, below the fields, is a secondary button 'Save and add another' (name action, value add).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2873; DOM BUTTON value=add
claims.quote: Save and add another

claims.statement: With no documents saved, the region shows the empty-state message 'You have not added any documents yet.' below the 'Save and add another' button.
claims.quote: You have not added any documents yet.

claims.statement: Outside the region, the page's button group holds the primary 'Save and continue' button (name action, value continue).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2875; DOM BUTTON value=continue
claims.quote: Save and continue

claims.statement: The button group also holds a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button (name exit, value hub).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2849 DOM BUTTON name=exit value=hub
claims.quote: Save and return to overview

claims.statement: The button group ends with a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification overview.
claims.quote: Cancel and return to overview

claims.statement: No trace in this part presses 'Save and return to overview' or follows 'Cancel and return to overview', so what each saves and where it lands is not shown.
Saving a complete document with 'Save and add another' posts the form (multipart) and redirects back to the upload page (POST 302 to the same URL, then GET 200).
claims.quote: POST | .../accompanying-documents | 302 | .../accompanying-documents

claims.statement: After a successful add, the add-a-document fields are cleared: Document reference is empty again.
claims.quote: label="Document reference" toHaveValue("")

claims.statement: Saved documents are listed in a table inside the 'File upload' region (wrapper id documents-added), below 'Save and add another', with the visually hidden caption 'Documents you have added'.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3211 DIV#documents-added TABLE; region containment trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-299e5 call@2817
claims.quote: Documents you have added

claims.statement: The saved-documents table has the column headings 'Document reference', 'Document type', 'Date of issue', 'Status' and a fifth, visually hidden heading 'Actions'.
claims.quote: Document reference | Document type | Date of issue | Status | Actions

claims.statement: A saved row shows the reference as entered, the document type by its label (not its code) and the date of issue as dd/mm/yyyy, as entered.
claims.quote: GBHC1234567890 | Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) | 12/12/2025

claims.statement: A saved row does not show the uploaded file's name.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 rendered row; trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3211
claims.quote: ITAHC-2026-0001 | Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) | 03/01/2026 | Scanning for virus | Remove document 1
claims.note: Inferred from the rendered row cells: none carries the file name (itahc-upload.pdf).

claims.statement: Straight after saving, a row's Status cell shows a blue tag 'Scanning for virus', preceded by visually hidden text 'Virus check status for {reference}'.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 call@3257; DOM TD data-scan-status=PENDING
claims.quote: Virus check status for ITAHC-2026-0001 Scanning for virus

claims.statement: Once the scan finishes the row's tag changes to a green 'Check completed'.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 call@3261; rendered row on ?attempt=1
claims.quote: Check completed

claims.statement: The page knows four scan states and their tags: COMPLETE 'Check completed' (green), REJECTED 'Virus found' (red), PENDING 'Scanning for virus' (blue) and UNKNOWN 'Unknown' (grey).
claims.quote: {"COMPLETE":{"text":"Check completed","classes":"govuk-tag--green"},"REJECTED":{"text":"Virus found","classes":"govuk-tag--red"},"PENDING":{"text":"Scanning for virus","classes":"govuk-tag--blue"},"UNKNOWN":{"text":"Unknown","classes":"govuk-tag--grey"}}

claims.statement: When a scan completes, screen reader users hear 'Document scan complete: the file is safe to use' through a visually hidden polite live region.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 DOM #js-scan-status-announcer (aria-live=polite, aria-atomic=true, data-scan-copy COMPLETE.announcement)
claims.quote: Document scan complete: the file is safe to use

claims.statement: When a scan finds a virus, screen reader users are to hear 'Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again.'.
claims.quote: Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again.
claims.note: Present only as configuration in the DOM; no trace renders a rejected document.

claims.statement: No trace in this part shows a document whose scan finds a virus (or ends Unknown): the row, its tag, its actions and what Continue does then are not shown.

While a document is scanning, the page polls GET /accompanying-documents/status (JSON) about three seconds after loading and, once the scan settles, reloads itself at ?attempt=1 (the next settled link is ?attempt=2).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 network 17:36:19.861 GET page, 17:36:23.010 GET /status (application/json), 17:36:23.022 GET ?attempt=1; #js-scan-status-announcer data-settled-href
claims.quote: GET | .../accompanying-documents/status | 200 | application/json; charset=utf-8

claims.statement: While any document is scanning the page also holds a 'Refresh virus scan status' link to ?attempt=1 and the hint 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.', both hidden when scripts run.
claims.quote: Refresh virus scan status / Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.
claims.note: The refresh link is absent once every row is complete; no trace runs without scripts or reaches the timeout message.

claims.statement: A completed row's actions cell offers a 'View file' link with visually hidden text 'for document N', pointing at /accompanying-documents/{upload id}/file.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-1867c call@2983; rendered row in trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31
claims.quote: View file for document 1

claims.statement: A row that is still scanning shows no View file link, only Remove.
claims.quote: TD {"data-view-file-text":"View file","data-view-file-hidden":"for document 1"} BUTTON Remove document 1

claims.statement: Downloading a saved document returns 200 with content-type application/pdf, the body of the PDF, and the header x-content-type-options: nosniff.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-1867c test step pw:api@70 GET .../file; expect@71 to expect@74
claims.quote: content-type: application/pdf; x-content-type-options: nosniff

claims.statement: The download is served inline with cache-control no-cache and a content-disposition naming the file; through the configured stub the name is 'placeholder.pdf', not the name the trader uploaded.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-1867c network GET /accompanying-documents/f7e87592-.../file response headers
claims.quote: content-disposition: inline; filename="placeholder.pdf"

claims.statement: Each row's actions cell has a 'Remove' button styled as a link (govuk-link plus the non-govuk class app-link-button), with visually hidden text 'document N', submitting action=remove:{index}.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-182e4 call@2549; DOM BUTTON value=remove:0
claims.quote: Remove document 1
claims.note: app-link-button is outside govuk-frontend; a standard secondary/warning button or a link to a confirm page would stay inside the toolbox.

claims.statement: Remove deletes the row at once, with no confirmation page (POST 302 back to the upload page), and the empty-state message 'You have not added any documents yet.' returns when the last row goes.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-182e4 call@2549 to call@2553; network second POST 302
claims.quote: You have not added any documents yet.

claims.statement: A document can be removed while it is still scanning.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-182e4 call@2547 to call@2549 (remove clicked straight after the add, with no wait for Check completed)
claims.quote: click | .govuk-table__row >> has-text="ITAHC-2026-0001" >> button[name="Remove document 1"]
claims.note: Inferred from the timing: the test does not wait for the scan before removing.

claims.statement: Saved rows have no change or edit action: the trader can only view or remove a document.
claims.quote: View file for document 1 / Remove document 1
claims.note: Inferred from the actions the row renders.

claims.statement: 'Save and continue' with the add-a-document fields filled saves the document too: the POST redirects back to the upload page, which now shows the new row.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3209 to call@3211; network POST 302 -> /accompanying-documents
claims.quote: POST | .../accompanying-documents | 302 | .../accompanying-documents

claims.statement: After that continue the trader stays on the upload page while the document scans; pressing 'Save and continue' again once the row shows 'Check completed' leaves for the Overview.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3213 to call@3217; network POST ?attempt=1 302 -> overview
claims.quote: continue saves the document the trader filled in, then leaves once it is scanned
claims.note: Whether continue holds the trader back because of the pending scan or simply because a document was just added is not separated by the trace.

claims.statement: 'Save and continue' with only a document type chosen does not leave: the page re-renders (HTTP 400) with the error summary listing the missing reference, date and file, and the chosen type stays selected.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-e6cdc call@2437 to call@2447; network POST 400; selected option ITAHC
claims.quote: Enter a document reference / Enter a date of issue / Upload a document

claims.statement: 'Save and continue' with an untouched form leaves for the Overview (POST 302 to the overview): uploading documents is optional.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-a3d09 call@3303 to call@3305; network POST 302 -> overview
claims.quote: continue with an untouched form leaves the page, uploading being optional

claims.statement: After continuing with no documents, the overview's 'Upload documents' task stays 'To do' (blue tag).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-a3d09 call@3305 overview task list
claims.quote: Upload documents To do

claims.statement: After continuing with one scanned document, the overview's 'Upload documents' task, under the heading '4. Documents', shows 'Complete' (green tag).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3217 overview task list
claims.quote: 4. Documents ... Upload documents Complete

claims.statement: The error summary's title is 'There is a problem' and each message links to its field: #accompanyingDocumentReference, #accompanyingDocumentType, #accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue and #file.
claims.quote: There is a problem

claims.statement: Pressing 'Save and add another' with nothing filled in shows four errors, in field order: 'Enter a document reference', 'Select a document type', 'Enter a date of issue', 'Upload a document'.
claims.quote: Enter a document reference / Select a document type / Enter a date of issue / Upload a document

claims.statement: Each field in error carries the GOV.UK inline error pattern: govuk-form-group--error, a govuk-error-message with visually hidden 'Error:' prefix placed after the hint, the error id added to the control's aria-describedby, and the input's --error modifier.
claims.quote: P {"id":"accompanyingDocumentReference-error","class":"govuk-error-message"} Error: Enter a document reference

claims.statement: After a failed submit, a chosen file is not kept: the upload control reads 'No file chosen' again, while the typed reference and date are kept.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-77b8b rendered error page (reference ITAHC-ONE-TOO-MANY, date 03/01/2026, upload button 'No file chosen')
claims.quote: value=ITAHC-ONE-TOO-MANY ... value=03/01/2026 ... No file chosen

claims.statement: A notification holds at most 15 documents: fifteen documents can be added one after another with 'Save and add another'.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-77b8b call@3297 to call@3445 (ITAHC-CAPACITY-1 to ITAHC-CAPACITY-15)
claims.quote: up to a maximum of 15 files

claims.statement: Adding a sixteenth document is refused (HTTP 400) with the error 'You can upload a maximum of 15 files', whose summary link points at the saved-documents table (#documents-added).
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-77b8b call@3455 to call@3461; network final POST 400
claims.quote: You can upload a maximum of 15 files

claims.statement: The capacity error appears only in the error summary: no field shows an inline error message for it.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-77b8b DOM (no govuk-error-message or govuk-form-group--error)
claims.quote: <a href=#documents-added>You can upload a maximum of 15 files
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any inline error element in the trace's snapshots.

claims.statement: When the capacity error fires, the refused document's reference is kept in the Document reference field.
claims.quote: label="Document reference" toHaveValue("ITAHC-ONE-TOO-MANY")

claims.statement: Rows are listed in the order they were added and numbered from 1 in their hidden action text (Remove document 1 ... Remove document 15).
claims.quote: Remove document 1 ... Remove document 15

claims.statement: The empty upload page has no serious or critical axe accessibility violations.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-a1b9f call@3397 (axe run; test passed)
claims.quote: Empty document upload page

claims.statement: The upload page in its error state (empty add, error summary and #accompanyingDocumentType-error showing) has no serious or critical axe violations.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-c504b call@2913 to call@2919 (test passed)
claims.quote: Document upload error state

claims.statement: The open date of issue picker dialog has no serious or critical axe violations.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-01ae3 call@3249 to call@3253 (test passed)
claims.quote: Document date picker dialog

claims.statement: The upload page with a saved, scanned document has no serious or critical axe violations.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-43a1e call@2645 to call@2657 (test passed)
claims.quote: Populated document upload page

claims.statement: The file is uploaded with the form to the frontend itself; the onward hand-off to a document store and virus scanner (the 'configured stub' the test names) happens server side and does not appear in the browser's network log, so its call shape is not shown.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 network log (only localhost:3000 calls)
claims.quote: uploads through the configured stub and renders the saved row

claims.statement: Each saved document has an upload id (a UUID) the page carries on its status cell and in its file link.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3211 TD data-upload-id; trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-bbc31 View file href
claims.quote: data-upload-id="3c3a56c9-df63-464a-bdab-62b957f92d84"

claims.statement: Every page response (page, status poll and file) is sent with cache-control no-cache and x-content-type-options nosniff.
claims.quote: cache-control: no-cache; x-content-type-options: nosniff

claims.statement: No trace in this part revisits the upload page from the overview after documents are saved, so whether saved rows and their scan states persist across visits is not shown directly.

The page's components are govuk-frontend throughout (back link, caption, heading, tag, summary card, form group, label, hint, input, select, file upload, button, button group, table, details, error summary) plus the MOJ date picker; the only non-govuk classes are app-journey-strip and app-link-button.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-0b0a7 call@2849 class inventory of main; trace documents-fit-upload.fit-d-876de call@3211
claims.quote: app-journey-strip ... moj-datepicker ... govuk-summary-card ... govuk-file-upload ... app-link-button

claims.statement: Adding a valid document with Save and add another posts the form and redirects back to the Upload documents page (post, redirect, get); the new row appears in the documents table.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-scan-status.-7c6fb network: POST /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-Z066WM/accompanying-documents 302 then GET 200; action call@2583
claims.quote: POST | /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-Z066WM/accompanying-documents | 302 | location /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-Z066WM/accompanying-documents

claims.statement: A newly saved document shows the status tag 'Scanning for virus' in blue while its virus scan is pending.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-scan-status.-7c6fb action call@2583 (Status cell); also trace documents-fit-scan-status.-770d5 action call@3101
claims.quote: Scanning for virus
claims.note: Rendered as govuk-tag govuk-tag--blue. The status cell carries data-scan-status="PENDING".

claims.statement: Each row's status cell starts with visually hidden text naming the document by its reference, so a screen reader hears which document the status belongs to.
claims.ref: trace documents-fit-scan-status.-7c6fb action call@2593; trace documents-fit-scan-status.-770d5 action call@3101
claims.quote: Virus check status for SCAN-SAFE-0001

claims.statement: The hidden 'Virus check status for <reference>' label sits outside the tag and stays in place when the status changes, so it names the document in the pending state and the settled state alike.
claims.ref: scan-status.fit.spec.js:79-100; trace documents-fit-scan-status.-770d5 action call@3103 (settled cell keeps the label node, tag replaced)
claims.quote: Virus check status for SCAN-SAFE-0001 Check completed

claims.statement: The service tracks four scan states for an uploaded document: PENDING, COMPLETE, REJECTED and UNKNOWN, each mapped to a tag text and colour on the page.
claims.quote: {"COMPLETE":{"text":"Check completed","classes":"govuk-tag--green","announcement":"Document scan complete: the file is safe to use"},"REJECTED":{"text":"Virus found","classes":"govuk-tag--red","announcement":"Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again."},"PENDING":{"text":"Scanning for virus","classes":"govuk-tag--blue"},"UNKNOWN":{"text":"Unknown","classes":"govuk-tag--grey"}}

claims.statement: A document whose scan is still pending has no View file link: its Actions cell offers only Remove.
claims.quote: SCAN-SAFE-0001 Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC) 3/1/2026 Virus check status for SCAN-SAFE-0001Scanning for virus Remove document 1

claims.statement: Pressing Save and continue while any document is still being scanned keeps the trader on Upload documents and shows an error summary saying they cannot continue.
